sentences.text:
Heard Sri Kumar Vijay Singh, Advocate holding brief of Sri A.K. Yadav, Advocate for revisionist
and learned A.G.A. for State.
2.  This criminal revision under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C., has been filed aggrieved by the judgments and orders dated 22.08.1992 and 15.12.1993.

The Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kanpur Dehat vide order dated 22.08.1992 convicted revisionist and sentenced him to undergo three months rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs. 500/- under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954 (hereinafter referred to as ?Act, 1954?).
Thereagainst, revisionist preferred Criminal Appeal No. 39 of 1992 and Appellate Court while dismissing appeal, confirmed order of conviction and sentence passed by Trial Court.
Being aggrieved the revisionist preferred present revision.

3. It is contended that disputed food item has not been examined and not found adulterated and only on the ground that revisionist could not show any licence for selling the same, he has been Kishori Lal vs State Of U.P. on 1 August, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174042080/
1 convicted under Section 7/16 of act, 1954 though under Act, 1954 there is no provision of licence for selling Khowa and, therefore, offence under Section 7/16 is not made out.
4.

entities.text: Kishori Lal vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When questioned, learned A.G.A. could not show any provision under Act, 1954 requiring any licence for sale of Khowa and that be so, impugned judgment and order cannot sustain.
5. In the result, revision is allowed.
Impugned judgment and order dated 22.08.1992 and 15.12.1993 are hereby set aside.
6. Certify this judgment to the lower Court immediately.
